title: Egyptian Koshari
subtitle: Egyptian street food of lentils, rice, and pasta in spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Koshari is Egypt's national dish -- a layered bowl of rice, lentils, and pasta topped with a tangy tomato sauce and crispy fried onions. Each component is made separately and assembled to order. It is filling, cheap, and extraordinary in the combination of textures.
sourceNotes: Koshari is considered Egypt's national dish. It developed in the 19th century from a mix of Indian dal, Italian pasta brought by colonial traders, and Egyptian spiced tomato sauce. It is sold from specialist koshary restaurants and street carts throughout Egypt.

recipe.batchNotes: Make the components in large batches and assemble as needed. Components keep in the fridge for 3 days.

content.text: The crispy fried onions are the most important part of koshari. Slice the onions as thin as you can and fry them until deeply golden and almost jammy. They can be made a day ahead and kept in an airtight container.

items.prepNote: use small pasta like ditalini, elbow, or broken spaghetti

content.text: Cook the lentils in a pan of salted boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes until soft. Drain and set aside.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until just tender. Drain well.

Make the tomato sauce: cook the onion in 2 tbsp of oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin. Cook 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, vinegar, chilli flakes, and 0.5 tsp salt. Simmer for 12 minutes until thick.
Make the crispy onions: fry the sliced onions in the oil over medium heat for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
To assemble: layer rice, then lentils, then pasta in each bowl. Spoon over the tomato sauce. Top with crispy onions. Serve with extra sauce on the side.

items.cause: Not enough oil or not cooked long enough
items.fix: Use plenty of oil and cook until they are a deep mahogany colour before draining
Add a small pinch of sugar and simmer for another 2 minutes
Always rinse basmati rice until the water runs clear to remove excess starch

content.text: Koshari is sold from dedicated koshary restaurants found on almost every street in Cairo and across Egypt. It has no close equivalent anywhere else. The combination of rice, lentils, pasta, and tomato sauce sounds unlikely but the result -- especially with the crispy onions -- is far better than the sum of its parts.
